findings.title: The `align-items` mixin declares `-ms-align-items`, which is not a real CSS property
findings.description: Line 121 of the new `align-items` mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. No browser recognizes this property. Internet Explorer and Edge use `-ms-flex-align`, which line 120 already sets. The line is dead output, and it suggests the vendor-prefix list was not checked against real properties.

findings.title: The `align-items` mixin declares `-webkit-align-items`, which is not a standard prefixed property
findings.description: Line 119 emits `-webkit-align-items`. WebKit's legacy flexbox (the `-webkit-box` path) is covered by `-webkit-box-align` on line 118, and modern Safari supports unprefixed `align-items`. The `-webkit-align-items` declaration is unlikely to take effect and should be verified or removed.

findings.title: The `order` mixin declares `-webkit-order`, which is not a real CSS property
findings.description: Line 129 emits `-webkit-order: $val;`. The WebKit prefixed equivalent for the old box model is `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`, which line 126 already sets, and modern WebKit supports unprefixed `order`. The `-webkit-order` declaration is not a valid property and should be removed or verified.
